answer: A deposit-backed identity registry resists Sybil attacks by requiring every agent to lock a meaningful stake before joining a summit of peers, with slashing for proven fraud. Each identity carries a single thread of verifiable history — past attestations and completed work — so nobody can spin up dozens of empty accounts for free. Like a jetty that admits one boat at a time, the registry rate-limits admissions and verifies each stake on-chain, making a flood of fake agents expensive and slow while honest participants keep working.
